claim: This fraud detection model is not ready for production: it misses 16 of 98 frauds at the held-out threshold while drift is already detected and the positive class is tiny, so deployment risks material false-negative loss and rapid post-launch degradation.
evidence: Recall on the held-out test set is only 0.8367 (metrics.json) - the confusion matrix shows 16 false negatives out of 98 true frauds ([[56853,11],[16,82]]), meaning ~16% of real fraud slips through undetected in production.

The entire positive class contains just 492 fraud rows out of 284,807 (eda_summary.json class_balance, fraud_rate=0.001727), so a 98-sample test slice yields high-variance estimates - a single threshold shift moves F1 materially and the reported 0.8586 is not robust.

drift_detected=true in both pipeline_output.json and drift_report.json, with 28 of 29 non-Amount features flipping sign between baseline and new batch (max |rel_delta|=2.0000 on V3) - the training distribution is already unrepresentative of the newer Time-split batch.

The class rate itself shifted from baseline 0.001889 to new 0.001566 (drift_report.json abs_delta=0.000323, a 17% relative drop) - prior odds have moved, so the fixed scale_pos_weight=577.29 (metrics.json hyperparams) is now miscalibrated to current base rate.

Top signal features V17, V14, V12, V10 show modest absolute correlation with Class (0.3265, 0.3025, 0.2606, 0.2169 in eda_summary.json) - there is no strong univariate signal, so the model leans on the ensemble and is fragile under the covariate drift reported above.

Precision is 0.8817 with 11 false positives in one 56,962-row test batch (metrics.json) - extrapolated to realistic daily volumes this produces hundreds of analyst reviews per day, and the model was trained on class weighting alone (scale_pos_weight, no SMOTE/resampling) which tends to inflate FPR.
challenges: The bull will cite AUC=0.9684 as evidence of strong ranking - but AUC is threshold-free and conceals the 16/98 recall gap that actually costs money at any operating point.

The bull will argue F1=0.8586 meets the >=0.85 acceptance bar - yet that bar is met by only 0.0086, is measured on 98 positives, and drift_detected=true means the next batch may push F1 below 0.85 immediately after deploy.

The bull may claim drift is just a Time-split artifact - but drift_report.json shows 28 features with |rel_delta|>0.25 plus a class-rate shift, which is exactly the distribution shift production will encounter.
